TRACE: LoCoMo Hypergraph Explorer
About this figure — click to collapse

What you are looking at

An interactive view of a 3-level hierarchical hypergraph extracted from one long-context dialogue. Each sample in the dropdown is one full conversation (months of dialogue between two speakers). The graph encodes the events extracted from that conversation, the sessions they belong to, and the topics that group sessions together.

Level 2 topic [LLM-clustered groups of sessions, 3-7 per sample] | topic_contains / belongs_to_topic Level 1 session [one chat session; star-expanded over its events] | contains / belongs_to Level 0 event [an action / state_change / preference / plan extracted from the session summary, with time anchor]

Legend

Event nodes (Level 0) — shape + color
●action (circle)
▲state_change (triangle)
◆preference (diamond)
★plan (star)
stale (valid_until set; gray fill, dashed border, strikethrough label)
Edges — color + dash pattern
causes (solid red)
enables (long-dash green)
prevents (dotted orange)
temporal_before (thin solid gray)
updates (thick solid blue)
contradicts (medium-dash magenta)
belongs_to / contains (short-dash hyperedges)

Reading the numbers

  • events / sessions / topics: counts of nodes at each level.
  • edges: total directed edges, semantic + hyperedges combined.
  • Stale events (valid_until set) render at opacity 0.4 with gray fill, dashed border, and strikethrough label — four redundant cues for colorblind / grayscale viewing. The valid_until timestamp shows on hover (and in the click panel).

How to use

  1. Pick a sample from the dropdown to switch to that conversation.
  2. Toggle topics / sessions / events to fold or unfold each layer.
  3. Toggle individual semantic edge types to focus on one causal pattern at a time. temporal_before is off by default because it is the densest type.
  4. Click any node to see its full attributes (participants, time anchor, provenance, validity) in the bottom panel.
  5. Drag to pan; scroll to zoom; drag a node to repin it.
  6. Drag the Time slider to scrub through the conversation: the view shows every event and session whose time anchor is on or before the cursor (cumulative). Click All to restore the full graph. Events with fuzzy time anchors (e.g. future, last year, summer 2023) cannot be ordered and stay visible at every cursor position.
  7. Click Fit to refit the camera to all currently visible nodes (useful after dragging nodes off-viewport or after toggling layers).
  8. Click PNG to download the current canvas as a PNG snapshot named graph_sample_N.png, for use in review notes.

Highlight a stress-test path

The Stress path input lets you visualise the BFS path the retrieval pipeline produced for a specific update-heavy QA case from the evaluation benchmark (59 cases across all 10 conversations). Type a stress_NNN id and press Highlight — the view auto-switches to the source conversation, draws a red border on the path's event nodes, thickens the path edges in red, and fits the camera. The bottom panel then shows the question, reference answer, the outdated answer the system has to override, and what the model actually predicted (with F1 against the reference).

Two illustrative cases:

  • stress_034 — fact_override on sample 5, F1 = 1.00. A clean positive: the BFS path traverses an updates edge and arrives at the current valid fact.
  • stress_044 — temporal_correction on sample 7, F1 = 0. A failure case: the BFS path is captured but the prediction misses the temporal correction. Useful for inspecting where path-based retrieval breaks down on update-dense queries.
